correctness.rationale: The six-dimensional nilradical bracket is reconstructed by direct multiplication and gives three exterior equations. For b=0, rank at most two symplectic frames are parametrized by the irreducible rational Lagrangian Grassmannian LG(2,4), with the dimension 3r+3. For b nonzero, λ,μ variables yield either affine Z_r (a=c=0; dimension 4r) or an irreducible rational vector bundle R_r (dimension 3r+3). Explicit rank-three witnesses for r>=3 prove pairwise noncontainment, so these are all components. Finite-field counts follow by enumerating isotropic lines, Lagrangian planes, and surjective linear fibers; verified brute-force cases include all F2 triples and independent F4 adjoint-rank enumeration. The proof makes no characteristic exclusion, and finite computations are not used as infinite proofs.

originality.rationale: The new statement determines all three geometrically irreducible components for every r>=3, their dimensions and rationality, plus the exact polynomial number of commuting r-tuples over each finite field. Goodwin-Röhrle (arXiv:1209.1289, §3.3) handles only r=2 with two components; Ngo (arXiv:1401.6820, Props. 3.1.2 and 3.2.2) establishes one regular component and non-equidimensionality for r>3, without an all-component formula or exact tuple counts. Li (arXiv:2403.13953) concerns commuting pair schemes and surface-group commutator relations. The closest indexed results concern other Lie algebras or different invariants and do not imply this claim. Residual historical priority risk remains, especially for implicit equivalent calculations.
residual_risks: An earlier equivalent formula might be implicit in nilradical orbit, determinantal, or symplectic frame literature rather than stated as a commuting-tuple theorem.
Basili DOI:10.1080/00927872.2016.1178272 full text was inaccessible; abstract concerns pairs, so current comparison remains qualified.

value.rationale: The component problem for commuting tuples is a motivating invariant in the cited Goodwin-Röhrle and Ngo literature. The exact r=3 three-component transition and the sharp r=4 onset of nonequidimensionality resolve substantially more than the known pair result or a general lower bound; the rational parametrizations and all-q tuple polynomial make the result a natural complete classification with arithmetic consequences, not an arbitrary finite slice. No broad downstream theorem is asserted.
